incoming.name: Copenhagen
incoming.excerpt: The element hafnium is named after the city's Latin name, Hafnia.

outgoing.name: Corrosion
outgoing.excerpt: Hafnium is a shiny silvery, ductile metal that is corrosion resistant and chemically similar to zirconium.

outgoing.name: Denmark
outgoing.excerpt: Hafnium (Latin Hafnia for "Copenhagen", the home town of Niels Bohr) was discovered by Dirk Coster and Georg von Hevesy in 1923 in Copenhagen, Denmark.

outgoing.name: Latin
outgoing.excerpt: Hafnium (Latin Hafnia for "Copenhagen", the home town of Niels Bohr) was discovered by Dirk Coster and Georg von Hevesy in 1923 in Copenhagen, Denmark.

outgoing.name: Mineral
outgoing.excerpt: A lustrous, silvery gray tetravalent transition metal, hafnium resembles zirconium chemically and is found in zirconium minerals.

outgoing.name: Niels Bohr
outgoing.excerpt: Hafnium (Latin Hafnia for "Copenhagen", the home town of Niels Bohr) was discovered by Dirk Coster and Georg von Hevesy in 1923 in Copenhagen, Denmark.

outgoing.name: Water
outgoing.excerpt: Minerals that contain zirconium, such as alvite [(Hf, Th, Zr)SiO4 H2O, thortveitite and zircon (ZrSiO4), usually contain between 1 and 5% hafnium.

outgoing.name: Norway
outgoing.excerpt: …finally found in zircon through X-ray spectroscope analysis in Norway.
